objective: Equity book v1.4 candidate: does an out-of-sample ML composite of the same 22 slow theme inputs plus log size (M2 GBDT rank-mean of LightGBM/XGBoost/CatBoost on the 21-session book-aligned label; M3 DKKM random-Fourier-feature ridge SDF, P = 4,000, on the 5-session book-aligned return), or an equal blend of M0 with either, raise the offset-median net Sharpe of the unchanged v1.2 construction (U3000) by >= 0.10 in both the recent 2024-01-08..2026-09-15 and the stress-ML 2019-01-02..2023-08-31 windows, with annual expanding refits from 2019, a 43-session embargo and the same costs, and does it survive the paired test, account layer, placebo and family-19 DSR tier?

sources.core_claim: Random-Fourier-feature ridge SDFs with P >> T earn out-of-sample SDF Sharpe near 3.7 (1993 onward, gross), about 2.6x low-complexity models; mega/large caps alone about 1.6/1.8 versus FF6 0.74.
sources.project_applicability: Exact form of M3 (eq. 6 and 9, gamma grid footnote 12, N^-1/2 scaling footnote 10), applied to our 23 slow inputs weekly.
sources.reflection: Gross of costs, microcap-driven headline, 130 characteristics and 30-year monthly windows; our version is much smaller and the cost question is ours to answer.

sources.core_claim: Complex models on economically motivated signals improve out-of-sample gross Sharpe 50-100% (65% in liquid large caps) and are highly additive to the simple model; two noisy predictors halve performance.
sources.project_applicability: Fixes the input set to economically motivated themes and motivates the M0+ML blends.
sources.reflection: Hypothetical, gross, 1963-2019; the cost effect is explicitly left open.

sources.core_claim: In the 500 largest stocks, ML forecasts do not beat linear Fama-MacBeth forecasts after costs; turnover-penalised risk-targeted portfolios reach net Sharpe 1.10-1.20 with the linear forecasts.
sources.project_applicability: Contrary prior: lowers the chance that M2/M3 replace M0; supports keeping M0 in the blends and the paired-test requirement for replacement.
sources.reflection: Preliminary paper; monthly mean-variance construction differs from our rank-weighted weekly book.

sources.core_claim: Jensen, Kelly, Malamud and Pedersen (SFI 22-63, 2022 version; RFS 2026): portfolios that put ML return forecasts, risk and trading costs into one objective keep positive out-of-sample net Sharpe ratios, reaching 1.38 for Portfolio-ML for an investor whose wealth reaches $10 billion by 2020, while cost-agnostic Markowitz portfolios fall to negative net returns.
sources.project_applicability: Sets the realistic ceiling for a cost-aware book and supports one optimizer holding alpha, risk and costs (design section 8); M3 (random-feature ridge) follows this line. v1.3: eq. (20) starts from the grown (drifted) position and trades toward an aim, the form of rules P2/P3/P2V.
sources.reflection: 2022 working-paper version (the RFS 2026 numbers may differ); price-impact costs only; a $10 billion large-cap investor, not a $1M U3000 book; the full model set needs about 75 GB, so we run a reduced version.

sources.core_claim: AQR Alternative Thinking 2023 Issue 4, Exhibit A1 (Hedge Fund Research data, May 1996 - August 2023, net of fees, 87 systematic and 337 discretionary long/short equity funds including dead funds): systematic funds' Sharpe ratio is 0 / 0.2 / 0.51 / 0.87 / 1.18 at the 10th / 25th / median / 75th / 90th percentile, with median beta 0.08.
sources.project_applicability: Calibrates the target: a book net Sharpe of 0.5-1.0 is the professional median to 75th percentile, and K1's 1.19 anchor bar sits at the systematic 90th percentile.
sources.reflection: Manager-written note; fund returns are net of fees while our book has no fees but no institutional execution either; global funds, not US-only; exact publication date not printed in the snapshot.

sources.core_claim: Chen and Velikov (JFQA 58(3), May 2023): after effective bid-ask spreads, post-publication decay and restricting to the post-2005 trading-technology era, the average published anomaly is expected to earn just 4 bp per month net; the strongest anomalies net at best about 10 bp, and several methods for combining anomalies net around 20 bp.
sources.project_applicability: Single anomalies are not worth trading alone after costs; only cost-aware combinations can clear the bar, which is why the book replaces standalone anomaly tests.
sources.reflection: Spread costs only (no impact, no short-sale fees); anomaly portfolios as published; the date is the issue month.

sources.core_claim: Jensen, Kelly and Pedersen (JF 2023): on a new global data set of 153 factors across 93 countries, most asset pricing factors can be replicated, cluster into 13 themes and work out of sample.
sources.project_applicability: Supports theme-level composites (M0 equal-weights themes) and the theme list of signal library v1.
sources.reflection: Gross factor returns; replication is not net profitability (see Chen-Velikov); the snapshot does not print the issue date.

sources.core_claim: Alpaca margin and short-selling documentation (fetched 2026-10-02): a Reg T margin account may hold up to 2x equity in marginable securities overnight and receives a margin call the next morning if initial (50%) and maintenance requirements are not met at the end of the day; maintenance is 30% for longs above $6 and the greater of $5.00/share or 30% for shorts at $5 or more; easy-to-borrow shares carry $0 locate and borrow fees for Trading API users while hard-to-borrow shorts need an approved locate; margin interest is 5.00% (elite) or 6.50% (non-elite) on the end-of-day debit balance.
sources.project_applicability: Fixes the account layer of v1.2: total gross including the SPY hedge and the T-bill leg capped at 1.8x equity (Reg T 2x minus a 10% buffer), the Alpaca maintenance table for the end-of-day margin check, borrow 0 bp on easy-to-borrow shorts, debit interest 6.50% a year for F2.
sources.reflection: HTML page without a version date (published_or_updated_at unknown); rates and the ETB fee policy can change; paper accounts may not enforce every rule, so the simulation enforces them itself.
